features.name: useGraphData stable references (fix React #185 infinite topology loop)
features.behavior: Every function returned by useGraphData (createNode, updateNode, deleteNode, createEdge, updateEdge, deleteEdge, search, getTopology, exportGraph, importGraph) is wrapped in useCallback with correct deps, and the whole returned object is wrapped in useMemo, so consumers can safely put these functions in their own effect dependency arrays without retriggering on every render. Fixes a real production crash: toggling the topology overlay threw React error #185 ("Maximum update depth exceeded") because getTopology was a brand-new function literal on every render, and AppPage's topology useEffect had getTopology in its dependency array - each render the effect triggered created a new getTopology reference, which retriggered the effect, in an infinite loop; the effect's own .catch() swallowed the resulting failure and surfaced it as a misleading "Không tính được topology" alert instead of an obvious crash.
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/hooks/useGraphData.test.js src/pages/AppPage.test.jsx
features.evidence: Reported 2026-08-25 via a real-usage bug report (importing a VESTA progress-graph JSON). Verified the root cause directly in useGraphData.js before fixing (getTopology defined inline in the returned object literal, no memoization). Added a referential-stability regression test (useGraphData.test.js) and a full end-to-end integration regression test (AppPage.test.jsx, 'toggling topology does not enter an infinite update loop') that clicks the real 'Độ quan trọng' button through the real (non-mocked) useGraphData hook. Confirmed the integration test is a genuine regression test, not a false positive: ran it against the pre-fix useGraphData.js (via git stash) and it failed (the topology button disappeared from the DOM, consistent with the reported crash); ran it again against the fix and it passed. Full frontend suite after fix: npm run test -> 15 files, 90 passed (up from 14 files/80 passed). npm run build -> 611 modules, clean. npm run lint -> oxlint 0 warnings/0 errors, 40 files.

features.name: Mock-mode cluster recompute on structural graph changes
features.behavior: New frontend/src/clustering/mockClustering.js computes connected-component clusters ({cluster_id, node_ids}, same shape as the real backend's Louvain-based ClusterService). useGraphData's mock-mode createNode/deleteNode/createEdge/deleteEdge/importGraph now call this after any structural change (node/edge added or removed) and update the `clusters` state accordingly, instead of leaving `clusters` frozen on the hardcoded mockData.js demo clusters forever. Deliberately NOT recomputed on every nodes/edges change via a passive effect, and NOT recomputed on updateNode/updateEdge (field edits don't change graph topology) - see Decisions.md for why (the bundled demo graph is a fully-connected star that would collapse into one cluster under naive connected-components on every render).
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/clustering/mockClustering.test.js src/hooks/useGraphData.test.js
features.evidence: Reported 2026-08-25 alongside FE017 via the same VESTA-import bug report: importing a real 28-node/29-edge graph in mock mode rendered zero cluster hulls, because GraphCanvas.jsx's hullPathFor() looks up cluster.node_ids against ids that only exist in the hardcoded mockClusters ('p', 'c1', ...), which imported nodes (fresh crypto.randomUUID() ids) never match. Added mockClustering.test.js (6 tests: connected grouping, singleton isolation, disconnected components, dangling-edge tolerance, empty graph, partition invariant) and useGraphData.test.js regression tests asserting every current node id appears in exactly one cluster after importGraph/createNode/deleteNode. npm run test -> 15 files, 90 passed. npm run build -> 611 modules, clean. npm run lint -> 0/0, 40 files.

features.name: i18n foundation (vi/en/ja) + TopBar migration
features.behavior: Lightweight, dependency-free i18n layer: frontend/src/locales/{vi,en,ja}.json dictionaries; frontend/src/i18n/translations.js (pure lookup/interpolation helpers, no JSX); frontend/src/i18n/context.js (the React context object, default value works even outside a provider so components/tests can render in isolation); frontend/src/i18n/I18nContext.jsx (I18nProvider component only); frontend/src/i18n/useTranslation.js (the useTranslation() hook, in its own file so I18nContext.jsx exports only a component - keeps React Fast Refresh / oxlint's react(only-export-components) rule clean). App.jsx wraps the router in <I18nProvider>. TopBar.jsx fully migrated off hardcoded Vietnamese strings to t(...) calls, plus a real language <select> dropdown (VI/EN/JA) that persists the choice to localStorage (key bt-locale) and updates every visible label live. Default locale is 'vi', matching the app's prior hardcoded language, so no existing test needed to change. This is the foundation piece from a 3-part i18n plan (see report); TopBar is migrated as the proof-of-concept, other components (NodeForm, EdgeForm, NodeDetailPanel, SearchBar, ImportExportControls, auth/landing pages) are NOT yet migrated - tracked as follow-up.
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/i18n/I18nContext.test.jsx src/components/TopBar.test.jsx
features.evidence: 2026-08-25, same VESTA-import bug report's Issue 3 (multilingual support vi/en/ja), Option A (custom lightweight context) chosen over i18next per the report's own recommendation, to avoid an extra dependency for a 3-language flat-key use case. Added I18nContext.test.jsx (8 tests: default-locale correctness, switching + localStorage persistence, restoring persisted locale, ignoring unsupported stored locale, interpolation, missing-key fallback, works without a provider, and a structural test asserting all 3 locale JSON files define the exact same key set so no language is silently missing a translation). Added TopBar.test.jsx (3 tests: default Vietnamese labels, full label swap across all 3 languages via the selector, error-message interpolation). Full frontend suite after change: npm run test -> 17 files, 101 passed (up from 15 files/90 passed after FE017/FE018). npm run build -> 618 modules, clean. npm run lint -> oxlint 0 warnings/0 errors, 46 files (previously 3 fast-refresh warnings during development, resolved by splitting context/translations/hook into separate non-JSX files - documented in Decisions.md). Backend suite unaffected, re-confirmed: pytest -q -> 118 passed, 1 skipped.

features.name: Universe visual theme system (starfield background, orbit motifs, space color tokens)
features.behavior: New base theme layer implemented: theme.js extended with universe-theme tokens (nebula[] gradient tints, orbitLine, starColor/starOpacityMin/Max, glow(color, strength) helper, cometDashArray) plus a deterministic seededRandom() helper - all existing tokens (canvasBg, panelBg, panelBorder, accent, depthColors, clusterPalette, etc.) kept as the same keys so every existing consumer (TopBar, GraphCanvas, all forms/pages) picks up the deepened space-black palette with zero code changes on their end. New Starfield.jsx component: canvas-based twinkling starfield (two depth layers for parallax-of-scale), CSS radial-gradient nebula glows, and SVG orbit-ring ellipses, mounted globally in App.jsx behind all routes. Respects prefers-reduced-motion (renders stars at fixed mid-brightness instead of animating). LandingPage's own opaque background removed so the global starfield shows through as the first visible use of the theme; AppPage's dense UI panels remain opaque over it by design. Foundational for FE023 (personalization), FE024 (marketing pages), and FE025 (3D graph), which all build their look on these same tokens/component.
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/theme.test.js src/components/Starfield.test.jsx
features.evidence: 2026-08-25. Implemented per the universe-theme roadmap (see Decisions.md 2026-08-25 entry) and the frontend-design skill's guidance: near-black-with-accent is flagged as a default cliche unless the brief specifies that direction, which it explicitly does here (universe theme requirement) - kept it distinctive by using the existing multi-hue palette as layered nebula depth rather than one flat accent, and by making the starfield the one deliberate 'signature' ambient element rather than decorating every surface. Added a requestAnimationFrame/cancelAnimationFrame polyfill to src/test/setup.js (jsdom has neither), following the file's existing polyfill convention (see the SVGSVGElement width/height entry already there). theme.test.js (7 tests): every pre-existing token still present, new tokens defined and correctly typed, glow() output format, colorForDepth still cycles correctly, seededRandom is deterministic/bounded/varies across seeds. Starfield.test.jsx (6 tests): renders and is aria-hidden, renders a canvas element, renders orbit-ring SVG ellipses, mounts/unmounts cleanly even when getContext('2d') returns null (jsdom's real behavior without the native 'canvas' package - explicitly simulated rather than relying on jsdom's actual behavior staying that way forever), respects prefers-reduced-motion (exactly one animation frame requested, not repeated), and cleans up its resize listener on unmount. Full suite after change: npm run test -> 19 files, 116 passed (up from 103 before this session). npm run build -> 619 modules, clean. npm run lint -> caught and fixed one real issue (unused STAR_COUNT constant left over from an earlier draft, superseded by per-layer counts) before landing at 0 warnings/0 errors, 49 files. Backend re-confirmed unaffected: pytest -q -> 118 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged).

features.name: 3D graph view with 2D/3D toggle button
features.behavior: A WebGL/three.js-rendered 3D force-directed graph view (client-side layout, same data shape as the existing 2D GraphCanvas), with a single toggle button in TopBar switching between the existing 2D GraphCanvas (FE008) and the new 3D view. Orbit-style camera controls (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom) matching the universe theme (FE022). No backend change required - 3D positions are computed client-side from the same /nodes and /edges data the 2D view already consumes (see F023 for the optional persistence extension).
features.verification: cd frontend && npm run test -- src/components/GraphCanvas3D.test.jsx
features.evidence: 2026-08-28. Implemented computeLayout() in src/graph3d/computeLayout.js (deterministic 3D force simulation using seededRandom, 200 iterations, pairwise repulsion + spring attraction + centering + damping). Implemented GraphCanvas3D.jsx (Three.js WebGL scene, OrbitControls with damping, glowing sphere node meshes, line segment edge meshes, selected node wireframe ring, pointer click-vs-drag distinction with raycaster hit-testing, safe null-WebGL jsdom fallback, and comprehensive geometry/material disposal on unmount). Lazy-loaded via React.lazy/Suspense in AppPage.jsx (main bundle 341.67 kB, GraphCanvas3D on-demand chunk 543.74 kB). TopBar gained 2D/3D toggle with full i18n support across vi/en/ja (view_2d/view_3d keys). Tests: computeLayout.test.js (7 tests), GraphCanvas3D.test.jsx (6 tests), AppPage.test.jsx 2D/3D toggle (1 test). Full suite: 21 files, 131 passed, build clean (624 modules), lint clean (0 errors/0 warnings on 53 files).
